::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Samsung's largest NAND flash site outside South Korea and a major share of its total NAND output (domestic Korean reporting put it around 40%) — the single biggest reminder that 'China's semiconductor sector' includes large-scale foreign-owned manufacturing on Chinese soil, not only domestic Chinese firms. Samsung reported a 67.5% year-on-year increase in Xi'an investment in its 2025 business report.
:::

**Chinese name:** 三星（中国）半导体有限公司 (Sānxīng (Zhōngguó) Bàndǎotǐ Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

3D NAND flash memory wafers; the fab has progressed from 128-layer (V6, now phased out) to 236-layer (V8, in mass production as of early 2026), with 286-layer V9 production targeted for later in 2026.

## Why does it matter?

A test case for how far US export controls reach into foreign multinationals' own China operations: Samsung ships significantly more semiconductor product to China than to the US by value, and continues to operate and upgrade Xi'an under an annual US tool-export licensing regime (replacing an earlier open-ended waiver) rather than a blanket ban.

## Technology Node Trajectory

- **2026**: 236-layer 3D NAND (V8)

## Project Timeline

- **Mar 2026** — Reported to be advancing Xi'an to 236-layer (V8) NAND in mass production
- **May 2026** — Reported to begin cleanroom build-out for V9 NAND infrastructure following the V8 ramp and V6 phase-out
